```{r, include = F}
# Set up the file we'll be using
ds <- read_csv("data-raw/raw_data.csv")
demo <- readxl::read_excel("data-raw/participant_demo.xlsx", sheet = "Data") %>% rename_all(janitor::make_clean_names)
ds <- ds %>% pivot_longer(-id, names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") %>% 
  mutate(condition = ifelse(str_detect(variable, "walk"), "walk", "search"),
         variable = str_remove_all(variable, "walk_"),
         variable = str_remove_all(variable, "search_"))
ds <- ds %>% pivot_wider(id_cols = c("id", "condition"), names_from = "variable", values_from = "value")
ds <- left_join(ds, demo, by = c("id" = "subject_number"))
ds <- ds %>% relocate(test_date:humidity, .after = condition) %>% mutate(humidity = as.numeric(humidity))
```

# CDA vs. EDA

- Goals of Confirmatory Data Analysis
  * Hypothesis testing, probabilistic modeling, inference
- Goals of Exploratory Data Analysis (Tukey)
  * Understanding the patterns in the data
  * Generating hypotheses
  * Checking your assumptions about data quality
  * “To find the unexpected, to avoid being fooled, and to develop rich descriptions” (Behrens & Yu, 2003)

.footnote[.small[.bold[[Behrens & Yu, 2013](https://psycnet.apa.org/record/2012-27075-002)]]]

---
# Why do we need EDA? 
- Summarizing = a loss of information
  * If you first look at summarized data (across trials, across participants, etc.), you may miss important patterns that exist at the raw data level
- Statistics without graphics can be misleading
  * Correlations without looking at the scatterplot
  * Means without examining outliers/distribution
  * Statistical tests without checking *N*

---
# Today's tutorial

- Ways to explore and check data
  * Part 1: Using tools we've already covered
  * Part 2: Using other packages: `DataExplorer`, `rstatix`
  * Part 3: Automating `ggplot2` plots to help understand your data
 
.content-box-blue[
`r icons::fontawesome("github")` Follow along from the [Github repo](https://github.com/2026-PSYC-259/7-exploratory-data-analysis)
]

.footnote[.small[.bold[Last updated: `r Sys.Date()`]]]

class: inverse, center, middle
# Part 1: EDA with tools you know

---
# Example data for today
```{r}
glimpse(ds)
```

---
# Things we already know how to do

- Use `glimpse()` to check that variables are correctly classed
- Use `filter()` to check for values outside expected boundaries
- Use logical statements to check assumptions
- Use `if`...`else` to print warnings
- Use `count()` to check frequencies
- Use `summarize()` to look at descriptive statistics

---
# Data checks using filters
```{r}
# Filter based on expected ranges
ds %>% select(id, age) %>% filter(age < 18 | age > 22)
# Filter based a set of possible values
ds %>% select(id, handedness) %>% filter(!(handedness %in% c("Right", "Left")))
```

---
# Print conditional warnings and errors
```{r}
# Filter based on expected ranges
check_age <- ds %>% select(id, age) %>% filter(age < 18 | age > 22)

if (nrow(check_age) > 0) print(str_glue("WARNING: {nrow(check_age)} participants have ages out of the expected range"))
```
---
# Print conditional warnings and errors
```{r}
# Filter based a set of possible values
check_handedness <- ds %>% select(id, handedness) %>% filter(!(handedness %in% c("Right", "Left")))

if (nrow(check_handedness) > 0) {
  print("Handedness check FAILED")
  print(check_handedness)
} else {
  print("Handedness check PASSED")
}
```

---
# Checking for expected counts
```{r}
# Check the number of participant ids
if (length(unique(ds$id)) != 30) print("ERROR: Incomplete Dataset")

# Count
count(ds, sex)
ds$sex <- tolower(ds$sex)

# Count NAs
sum(is.na(ds$temperature))
```
---
# Simple descriptive statistics
```{r}
ds %>% drop_na(temperature) %>% summarize(temp_min = min(temperature), temp_mean = mean(temperature), temp_max = max(temperature))

summary(ds$temperature) #Also a nice option
```

---
class: inverse, center, middle
# Part 2: EDA with other packages

---
# Other helpful packages: rstatix

- Pipe-friendly descriptive and inferential statistics (same author as ggpubr)
- `get_summary_stats` = flexible function for descriptive stats
- `freq_table` = Frequency tables with proportion
- `identify_outliers` = detects/filters outliers
- `cor_mat` and helper functions = correlation matrices and plots

---
# rstatix::get_summary_stats()
```{r}
# Get summary stats
ds %>% get_summary_stats(temperature) #Note that it drops NAs
ds %>% group_by(target, sex) %>% get_summary_stats(temperature)
```

---
# rstatix::get_summary_stats()
```{r}
# Specify multiple variables and types of output stats
ds %>% get_summary_stats(c("temperature", "humidity"), type = "common")

ds %>% get_summary_stats(starts_with("eyex"), type = "mean_sd")
```

---
# rstatix::freq_table()
```{r}
ds %>% freq_table(sex)

ds %>% freq_table(target, sex)
```
---
# rstatix::identify_outliers()
```{r}
if (nrow(identify_outliers(ds, temperature)) == 0) print("No temperature outliers")

ds %>% identify_outliers(eyex_mean) %>% select(id, condition, eyex_mean)
```
---
# rstatix::cor_mat()
```{r}
ds %>% cor_mat(starts_with("eyex_")) %>% pull_lower_triangle()

ds %>% cor_mat(starts_with("eyex")) %>% cor_plot()
```

---
# Other helpful packages: DataExplorer

- Quickly generate EDA plots for every column in your dataset
- `plot_histogram` and `plot_density` for continuous variables
- `plot_bar` for categorical
- `plot_boxplot` for detecting outliers
- `plot_missing` for missingness
- `plot_correlation` for between-column correlations at a glance
- `create_report` for everything

---
## Data Explorer: Histograms
```{r}
ds %>% select(condition, gazex_std:posy_speed) %>% plot_histogram()
```

---
## Data Explorer: Density plots
```{r}
ds %>% select(condition, gazex_std:posy_speed) %>% plot_density()
```

---
## Data Explorer: Boxplots by condition
```{r}
ds %>% select(condition, gazex_std:posy_speed) %>% plot_boxplot(by = "condition")
```

---
## Data Explorer: Plot missing
```{r}
ds %>% select(id:humidity) %>% plot_missing()
```

---
## Data Explorer: Correlations
```{r}
ds %>% select(gazex_std:posy_speed) %>% plot_correlation()
```

---
## Data Explorer: Create Report

- `create_report()` is a brute force approach, which makes every imaginable plot

```{r, eval = F}
ds %>% create_report()
# Saves an html report to your working directory
```

class: inverse, center, middle
# Part 3: Making your own EDA plots

---
# Using `ggplot2`

- Parts of a ggplot call:
```{r, eval = F}
# Parts of a ggplot call
ggplot(DATASET, aes(MAPPING STATEMENT)) + 
  geom_TYPE() + 
  geom_TYPE() + 
  ETC... + 
  OTHER_FORMATTING() #axes, labels, legends, themes, etc.
```
- Note that ggplot uses `+`, not `%>%`

---
# What type of aesthetic mapping depends on what type of geom

.center[![image](geoms.png)]

---
# What type of aesthetic mapping depends on what type of geom
- `?geom_point` and scroll down to find required aesthetics in bold
.center[![image](aesthetics.png)]

---
`r chunk_reveal("geoms", break_type = "rotate", widths = c(1, 1), title = "Distribution plots to check ranges")`

```{r geoms, include = FALSE}
ds %>% mutate(age = ifelse(id == 103, 30, age)) %>% 
ggplot(aes(x = age)) + 
  geom_histogram() + #ROTATE
  geom_density() + #ROTATE
  geom_boxplot() + #ROTATE
  xlab("Age (years)")
```

---
`r chunk_reveal("categorical", float = "none", break_type = "rotate", widths = c(2, 1), title = "Add a category")`

```{r categorical, include = FALSE}
ggplot(ds) + 
 geom_boxplot(aes(y = posy_std)) + #ROTATE 
 geom_boxplot(aes(x = condition, y = posy_std)) + #ROTATE
 geom_boxplot(aes(x = condition, y = posy_std, fill = condition)) + #ROTATE
 geom_boxplot(aes(x = condition, y = posy_std, fill = target)) #ROTATE
```

---
`r chunk_reveal("scatterplot", break_type = "auto", widths = c(1, 1), title = "Simple scatterplot")`

```{r scatterplot, include = FALSE}
ggplot(ds, aes(x = posx_mean, y = posy_mean)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  xlim(-20, 20) + 
  ylim(-20, 20) + 
  xlab("Mean horizontal head position") + 
  ylab("Mean vertical head position") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0)
```

---
`r chunk_reveal("facet", break_type = "auto", widths = c(1.5, 1), title = "Facetting a scatterplot")`

```{r facet, include = FALSE}
ggplot(ds, aes(x = posx_mean, y = posy_mean)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  facet_wrap("condition", ncol = 2)
```

---
`r chunk_reveal("saving", break_type = "auto", widths = c(1.5, 1), title = "Saving plots")`

```{r, saving, include = F}
ggplot(ds, aes(x = posx_mean, y = posy_mean)) + geom_point()
#ggsave will save the last plot to file
ggsave("eda/head-position-scatter.jpg")

#You can also save plots to objects (they are lists)
p1 <- ggplot(ds, aes(x = posx_mean, y = posy_mean)) + geom_point()
ggsave("eda/head-position-scatter.jpg", plot = p1)
```

---
# Useful ggsave options

- `width`, `height`, and `units` = specify the size of the saved plot
- `device` = "png", "eps", "pdf" (but will choose based on filename)
- `scale` = bump up the scale (1.5) if the text/lines look too big or down (.5) if text/lines look too small

`ggsave("eda/output.pdf", units = "in", height = 4, width = 4, scale = .75)`

---
# Automation + plotting

- Each plot you create appears in the plots tab in RStudio

- Flipping through a few plots is OK, but not hundreds

- Write plotting functions that can save plots to file to better organize them

---
# Automation + plotting
```{r}
plot_dv_by_condition <- function(dv) {
  ggplot(ds, aes(fill = condition, y = .data[[dv]])) + 
    geom_boxplot()
}
plot_dv_by_condition("posx_std")
plot_dv_by_condition("posy_std")
```
---
# Why does that work?

- `ds %>% .[["posx_std"]]` is the same as `ds$posx_std`
- Double brackets let you access the column by character name
- `.data` is a ggplot shortcut for 'the current data'
- `y = .data[[dv]]` says 'use the name in dv to choose the y column'

---
# Make the function more useful with labels/saving
```{r}
plot_dv_by_condition <- function(dv) {
  p <- ggplot(ds, aes(fill = condition, y = .data[[dv]])) + 
    geom_boxplot() + 
    ylab(dv) + #we can also use dv to label the axis
    ggtitle(str_glue("{dv} by condition")) + #and title the plot
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  # and we can use it to write a sensible output filename
  ggsave(str_glue("eda/by_condition/{dv}_by_condition_boxplot.jpg"), plot = p,
         height = 6, width = 4, units = "cm", scale = 2)
  return(p)
}
plot_dv_by_condition("posx_std")
```
---
# Use colnames() to get each of the dv characters
```{r}
dvs_to_plot <- ds %>% select(-(id:humidity)) %>% colnames
dvs_to_plot
walk(dvs_to_plot, plot_dv_by_condition)
```

---
# What if we want to specify the type of plot?
```{r}
plot_dv_by_condition <- function(dv, geom = "boxplot") {
  # Start of the ggplot
  p <- ggplot(ds) + 
    ylab(dv) + 
    ggtitle(str_glue("{dv} by condition")) + 
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  
  # Add the geom based on the text argument
  if (geom == "boxplot") p <- p + geom_boxplot(aes(fill = condition, y = .data[[dv]]))
  if (geom == "density") p <- p + geom_density(aes(color = condition, x = .data[[dv]]))
  ggsave(str_glue("eda/by_condition/{dv}_by_condition_{geom}.jpg"), plot = p,
         height = 6, width = 4, units = "cm", scale = 2)
  return(p)
}
```
---
# What if we want to specify the type of plot?
```{r}
plot_dv_by_condition(dv = "posx_std", geom = "boxplot")
walk(dvs_to_plot, ~ plot_dv_by_condition(dv = .x, geom = "boxplot"))
```

---
# What if we want to specify the type of plot?
```{r}
plot_dv_by_condition(dv = "posx_std", geom = "density")
walk(dvs_to_plot, ~ plot_dv_by_condition(dv = .x, geom = "density"))
```


---
# Automation + plotting with two variable inputs
```{r}
two_var_scatter <- function(df, var1, var2) {
  p <- ggplot(df, aes(x = .data[[var1]], y = .data[[var2]])) + 
    geom_point() + 
    xlab(var1) + 
    ylab(var2) + 
    ggtitle(str_glue("{var1} by {var2}"))
  ggsave(str_glue("eda/scatter/{var1}_{var2}.jpg"), plot = p,
         height = 7, width = 7, units = "cm", scale = 1.5)
  return(p)
}
two_var_scatter(ds, "posx_std", "posy_std")
```

---
# Get x and y pairs from colnames
```{r}
pred_x <- ds %>% select(matches("x_")) %>% colnames
pred_x
pred_y <- ds %>% select(matches("y_") & where(is.numeric)) %>% colnames
pred_y
pred_x_by_y <- map2(pred_x, pred_y, ~ two_var_scatter(ds, .x, .y))
pred_x_by_y
```

---
# Pivoting and faceting to automate plots
```{r}
ds_long <- ds %>% select(matches("x_")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything())

slice_head(ds_long, n = 7)
```

---
# Pivoting and faceting to automate plots
```{r}
ds_long %>% ggplot(aes(x = value)) + 
  geom_histogram() + 
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free", nrow = 2)
```
